transitions.title: Grade 5 and grade 8 science assessment cutover
transitions.finding: New NYSP12SLS elementary/intermediate science tests first administered in spring 2024; science remains represented in every grade, not only assessment years.

transitions.title: Biology and Earth/Space science assessment cutover
transitions.finding: New Life Science: Biology and Earth and Space Sciences Regents exams began June 2025. Legacy Living Environment and Physical Setting/Earth Science ended June 2026.

transitions.title: Chemistry and Physics assessment transition
transitions.finding: New Physical Science: Chemistry and Physics Regents exams began June 2026. Legacy Physical Setting/Chemistry and Physics continue through June 2027 for matching prior instruction; course/exam/reference-table versions must remain explicit.

transitions.title: Full CSDF implementation
transitions.finding: Full implementation began September 1, 2024. Students must achieve standards by the end of K–1, 2–3, 4–6, 7–8 and 9–12 bands; delivery and annual sequence remain local.

transitions.title: Climate education regulation permanently effective
transitions.finding: Permanent regulation effective March 25, 2026 with later phased instructional requirements. Early implementation is permitted; existing science climate content already applies.

transitions.title: Climate education phase-in for middle and high school
transitions.finding: Beginning in 2027–28, instruction is required within grades 5–8 by the end of grade 8 and grades 9–12 by the end of grade 12; school district/charter verification is required during phase-in.

transitions.title: Climate education phase-in for elementary school
transitions.finding: Beginning in 2028–29, instruction is required within K–4 by the end of grade 4; do not substitute a K–5 band or describe this as an already-required 2026–27 sequence.

review_notes.finding: A 2026–27 applicability review is not a new standards edition. State expectations and course maps permit local curricula, instructional methods and sequences.
Science tutoring should combine disciplinary ideas, scientific/engineering practices and crosscutting reasoning, rather than reducing coverage to isolated factual answers.

Required Regents Investigation materials are secure school-controlled content. Do not ingest secure teacher materials into public/shared tutoring corpora or expose teacher directions/answers to students. District-limited sharing rules apply; prerecorded Investigation tasks are prohibited.

General Regents laboratory experience may combine hands-on and simulated/virtual activities under the January 2023 rule, with 1,200 minutes and satisfactory documented reports. Required Investigations remain hands-on and must be successfully completed for matching Regents admission. A conversation alone does not certify school lab credit.
The reviewed official topics page still says detailed grade-band objectives are forthcoming. Catalog climate topic progressions are planning suggestions, not invented state objective identifiers.

NYS science standards contain state-specific additions. Later full teaching adapters must preserve authentic New York identifiers, course-specific scope, clarification statements and assessment boundaries.

Source review and subject representation do not approve teaching materials, teacher behavior or model use. School resources, current corpus snapshots and student-visible content retain separate approval/access controls.
